title: Claimed Lean-Formalized Proof of Subhash Khot’s Unique Games Conjecture
aiSystem: OpenAI Internal Frontier Math Model + Lean 4
whyItMatters: OpenAI’s internal model produced a Lean-formalized claimed proof of Subhash Khot’s 2002 Unique Games Conjecture via a novel “Hadamard with a noise test” code—unpacked by Dana Moshkovitz, Khot, Håstad, and Minzer.
summary: Released on October 6, 2026 as Family 102 of github.com/openai/math alongside a Lean 4 formalization, an internal OpenAI frontier reasoning model claimed a full proof of Subhash Khot’s 2002 Unique Games Conjecture—one of theoretical computer science’s most consequential open conjectures, implying optimal NP-hardness of approximation for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, and dozens of constraint satisfaction problems. After weeks of intensive collaborative scrutiny with Subhash Khot, Johan Håstad, and Dor Minzer, UT Austin complexity theorist Dana Moshkovitz presented a detailed November 4, 2026 seminar unpacking the core AI-discovered “Hadamard with a noise test” code construction.
technicalHighlights: Introduces a novel code construction—described by Dana Moshkovitz as “Hadamard with a noise test”—alongside a quadratic-behaving-like-linear ingredient and harmonic-number probability bound.
Accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization in OpenAI’s Family 102 repository plus related Family 105 (perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games).
Prompted intensive multi-week specialist verification by Dana Moshkovitz, Subhash Khot, Johan Håstad, and Dor Minzer, culminating in a Nov 4, 2026 UT Austin technical exposition.
caveats: Remains an unrefereed preprint under active community review. Specialists noted the original AI manuscript was extremely difficult for humans to parse without AI assistance, and final consensus requires full peer-reviewed verification that the Lean statement matches Khot’s exact conjecture without specification gaps.
contributors: Dana Moshkovitz, Subhash Khot, Johan Håstad & Dor Minzer (Audit & Exposition)
institutions: University of Texas at Austin (Audit Seminar)

scoreRationale.foundational: If fully certified, settles the central conjecture of hardness of approximation since Subhash Khot’s 2002 paper.
scoreRationale.ripple: Immediately upgrades dozens of UGC-conditional optimal inapproximability results (including Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut) into unconditional P ≠ NP consequences.
scoreRationale.verification: Includes a Lean 4 formalization and favorable initial specialist unpacking by Moshkovitz, Khot, Håstad, and Minzer, but formal refereeing is still ongoing.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomous discovery of a genuinely novel PCP/coding-theory construction in hours of frontier reasoning compute.
